meta.title: AutoR&D-Engineer on AutoResearchExam
meta.context: Selected Astra-based research campaigns combining AutoResearch and operator contributions.
meta.normalization: The benchmark website’s difficulty-adjusted reward mapping is used for both curves.
meta.selection: Checkpoint selection uses validation only. Hidden scores follow that selected checkpoint.
meta.coverage: Tasks randomly sampled by the research team to manage Astra evaluation cost (team-confirmed). Initial campaign: 21 CPU tasks; seven H100-only tasks excluded. This page highlights six selected results and four near-ties.
meta.gainNarratives: Every strict validation-best update after the initial checkpoint. Descriptions summarize cumulative implementations; timing remeasurements are identified. No isolated causal effect is claimed.
meta.safeguards: Original task graders and validation-only checkpoint selection; retained artifact/result hashes checked. Source, constraint, and access reviews are recorded. Independent certification by the benchmark publisher’s adversarial judge is not established.

tasks.title: Make every decoding step do less work.
tasks.goal: Generate text faster on an eight-core CPU while meeting the benchmark’s token-agreement requirement.

gains.title: Batch requests of the same length
gains.summary: Share decoding work across requests with matching sequence lengths.
gains.detail: Grouping compatible requests lets the model process them together. This reduces the repeated setup and small operations involved in generating each sequence separately.

gains.title: Allocate once, decode repeatedly
gains.summary: Combine batching with preallocated storage for repeated generation steps.
gains.detail: Keep the working buffers available across token steps instead of repeatedly constructing intermediate storage. The checkpoint combines this memory-management change with the earlier batching approach.

gains.title: Fuse the activation work
gains.summary: Use a fused GELU implementation inside the preallocated decoding path.
gains.detail: GELU is repeatedly applied in the feed-forward blocks. Fusing its work reduces intermediate operations while preserving the cumulative batching and buffer changes.

gains.title: Keep only active requests in the prefix
gains.summary: Let completed requests leave the batch without repeatedly copying the full cache.
gains.detail: Sort requests by length and keep live key/value caches in a contiguous prefix. Attention operates on that active prefix, avoiding work on completed sequences and repeated rearrangement of cache storage.

gains.title: Store weights for the operation that uses them
gains.summary: Retain transposed weights for the active-prefix decoding path.
gains.detail: Preparing the weight layout for repeated inference reduces layout handling in the hot path. This checkpoint keeps the earlier batching, caching, and attention choices.

gains.title: Move the model body onto AMX
gains.summary: Use specialized AMX matrix operations for the decoder body.
gains.detail: The implementation introduces a three-product AMX path for the repeated body computations. Hardware-specific matrix work is combined with the existing request scheduling and cache layout.

gains.title: Keep greedy selection in the native path
gains.summary: Add native greedy token selection to the accumulated AMX runtime.
gains.detail: Token selection happens at every decoding step. Keeping that work in the native implementation reduces repeated high-level dispatch around an otherwise accelerated model body.

gains.title: Adapt matrix tiles to the workload
gains.summary: Choose AMX tiling for the current computation shape.
gains.detail: A single tile configuration need not suit every decoding operation. This checkpoint adapts the matrix tiling while retaining the existing active-prefix runtime.

gains.title: Specialize the remaining bottlenecks
gains.summary: Combine a centered vocabulary head, direct attention, and selective cache initialization.
gains.detail: The vocabulary head uses a centered AMX computation. Direct attention kernels and sparse cache initialization address additional costs left after accelerating the main matrix operations.

gains.title: Combine native GELU with adaptive traversal
gains.summary: Carry the activation and matrix-traversal improvements into the complete runtime.
gains.detail: The checkpoint combines a native GELU path with cumulative adaptive AMX traversal. Its measurement covers the resulting end-to-end generation implementation.

gains.title: Test a residual INT8 model body
gains.summary: Use residual low-precision products to make the feed-forward computation cheaper.
gains.detail: This candidate raises the validation result, but its recorded hidden-test reward is zero. The next checkpoint refines the residual product scheme. Keeping this point in the replay preserves the actual research trajectory.

gains.title: Refine INT8 into four residual products
gains.summary: Recover more numerical detail while retaining cheaper matrix arithmetic.
gains.detail: Use a four-product residual INT8 body with the original small-matrix attention-projection fallback and centered BF16 vocabulary head. This checkpoint follows the earlier residual-INT8 experiment.

gains.title: Measure the accumulated runtime
gains.summary: Evaluate the retained implementation with its cumulative prefill and decoding changes.
gains.detail: The submitted artifact comes from the attempt’s baseline worktree. By this stage the retained runtime includes direct placement of prefill into the final key/value caches. This measurement is not evidence of a new code change at this checkpoint.

gains.title: Repeat the runtime measurement
gains.summary: The same production implementation records a higher validation speedup.
gains.detail: The source review found the production code and native libraries identical to checkpoint 18; only unused development helpers differed. This is a timing remeasurement, not a new algorithmic improvement.

gains.title: Skip unused final-block query projections
gains.summary: Only compute the prompt-query rows that the final block consumes.
gains.detail: Prune unused query projection rows during prefill in the final transformer block. The rest of the cumulative runtime is retained, and the candidate is evaluated as a complete generation implementation.

gains.title: Express causal attention directly
gains.summary: Avoid constructing an explicit prefill mask when the attention operator can express causality.
gains.detail: Use the installed scaled-dot-product attention operator’s causal mode in prefill. This builds on direct cache placement and final-query pruning; checks cover consumed state and continuation behavior.

gains.title: Re-evaluate the retained implementation
gains.summary: A later evaluation becomes the final validation-selected checkpoint.
gains.detail: The run labels this submission “initial-baseline” because it is the baseline for a later research stage. It is the evolved implementation, not the task’s original starting solution. Treat the recorded increase as a new measurement, not a newly identified method.

tasks.title: Turn a decoder graph into a lean execution engine.
tasks.goal: Execute transformer decoder graphs faster while preserving the required operations and numerical equivalence.

gains.title: Move graph execution into native kernels
gains.summary: Replace the packed Python path with an AVX-512 implementation.
gains.detail: The checkpoint moves numerical work into native vectorized code. Its end-to-end score measures graph execution under the task’s operation and numerical-equivalence requirements.

gains.title: Keep a worker pool alive
gains.summary: Reuse workers across native matrix-vector operations.
gains.detail: A persistent pool avoids repeatedly creating execution machinery around small operations. Matrix-vector kernels share the pool throughout graph execution.

gains.title: Use all eight workers
gains.summary: Extend the pooled execution path to an eight-worker configuration.
gains.detail: The checkpoint uses the available CPU workers in the native path. It builds on the persistent-pool implementation and is measured against the same task reference.

gains.title: Pack work for the matrix shape
gains.summary: Use a packed path specialized for the eight-row workload.
gains.detail: Packing related work gives the native kernel a layout suited to the evaluated matrix shape. This checkpoint retains pooled execution while changing how the matrix work is organized.

gains.title: Parallelize activation and attention
gains.summary: Apply the worker pool beyond the projection kernels.
gains.detail: Activation and attention remain on the execution path after matrix-vector work is accelerated. This checkpoint adds parallel work to those operations.

gains.title: Distribute independent rows
gains.summary: Partition row-level work across the available workers.
gains.detail: Independent rows provide another way to divide the graph’s numerical work. The candidate extends the earlier parallel activation and attention implementation.

gains.title: Fuse gate and activation work
gains.summary: Reuse intermediate values across operations that belong together.
gains.detail: Pack related projections and fuse gate/up activation work. The intent is to reduce separate passes and reuse data already being processed by the execution engine.

gains.title: Tile the fused kernel in blocks of 32
gains.summary: Test a different work partition for the fused gate path.
gains.detail: This checkpoint changes the fused computation’s tiling. The end-to-end measurement includes the existing worker pool, packing, and parallel operations.

gains.title: Refine the tile size to 48
gains.summary: Retune the fused kernel’s work partition for the measured workload.
gains.detail: The next candidate uses a 48-wide tile in the fused gate implementation. This is a kernel configuration refinement on the accumulated implementation.

gains.title: Vectorize activation and attention
gains.summary: Reduce scalar work in the remaining numerical kernels.
gains.detail: Vectorized activation and attention extend the native implementation beyond its matrix operations. The graph still performs the required attention computation.

gains.title: Pin workers to CPU cores
gains.summary: Make worker placement explicit.
gains.detail: Worker affinity controls where the persistent workers execute. This addresses scheduling and locality alongside the earlier arithmetic and tiling changes.

gains.title: Distribute worker completion signaling
gains.summary: Reduce contention in the synchronization path.
gains.detail: Use distributed completion signaling rather than making every worker depend on a single shared synchronization point. This checkpoint combines the change with the pinned worker pool.

gains.title: Tile full attention
gains.summary: Organize attention work into tiles of 32.
gains.detail: The implementation reorganizes full attention into smaller work units. It preserves the required attention operation while changing its execution layout.

gains.title: Refine the packed matrix-vector path
gains.summary: Carry an updated packed GEMV implementation into graph execution.
gains.detail: This checkpoint updates the packed matrix-vector kernel in the cumulative native engine. Its measurement reflects the complete graph, including the retained attention and worker coordination.

gains.title: Specialize attention for eight-way work
gains.summary: Match the full-attention kernel to the evaluated batch shapes.
gains.detail: The final selected implementation combines specialized attention with packed projections, fused activation, worker affinity, and distributed completion flags. The run ends at 3.92 hours; the plotted continuation holds this result constant.

tasks.title: Learn richer recommendations with just eight values.
tasks.goal: Improve held-out recommendation quality while keeping at most eight nonzero values in every item embedding.

gains.title: Learn first, then prune gradually
gains.summary: Train a richer representation and reduce it to eight nonzeros per item.
gains.detail: Replace a post-hoc spectral representation with reconstruction training in a 512-dimensional space and gradual top-k pruning. The deployed item vectors remain within the task’s eight-nonzero limit.

gains.title: Expand the training space to 4,096
gains.summary: Give reconstruction learning more room before enforcing sparsity.
gains.detail: Increase the latent training space while retaining gradual pruning. A larger space during learning does not change the eight-nonzero budget of each deployed item embedding.

gains.title: Learn in an 8,192-dimensional space
gains.summary: Continue scaling the representation used during sparse training.
gains.detail: The model trains in a larger latent space and retains a sparse output. Public holdout and fresh-mask checks precede the saved official checkpoint.

gains.title: Expand to 16,384 dimensions
gains.summary: Improve the trained sparse starting point for later refinement.
gains.detail: The checkpoint comes from a larger reconstruction-training run with the same public training data and deployment constraint. Later candidates refine this retained embedding rather than starting from scratch.

gains.title: Consider every slot when exchanging support
gains.summary: Choose sparse replacements using their effect on the normalized objective.
gains.detail: Compare renormalized deletion choices across the occupied slots instead of relying only on coefficient magnitude. Candidate support exchanges preserve the eight-nonzero constraint.

gains.title: Refine coefficients using recommendation context
gains.summary: Build context-aware updates on top of the retained sparse embedding.
gains.detail: The context-refinement stage extends the support-exchange runtime. The saved checkpoint measures the cumulative sparse representation after those updates.

gains.title: Focus refinement on reachable candidates
gains.summary: Use a reachable-candidate refinement stage while keeping support fixed.
gains.detail: The candidate updates the retained coefficients using a fixed-support refinement procedure. The checkpoint includes the earlier training, support-exchange, and context stages.

gains.title: Test an unweighted ranking refinement
gains.summary: Establish the equal-weight variant of a new ranking-oriented update.
gains.detail: This checkpoint is the unweighted arm of the ranking-refinement experiment. It retains the cumulative sparse runtime and provides a comparison for the weighted version.

gains.title: Weight refinement by ranking impact
gains.summary: Give the ranking objective a more direct role in sparse coefficient updates.
gains.detail: The weighted variant uses catalog-rank weighting with beta 0.5, building on the same retained representation. It slightly improves validation over the unweighted arm while preserving at most eight nonzeros per item.

tasks.title: Find a small set of points that covers space better.
tasks.goal: Select a subset with low star discrepancy: an even coverage of the unit cube within the task’s runtime budget.

gains.title: Start from a structured target
gains.summary: Use Sobol-based assignment to construct a more evenly spread subset.
gains.detail: A structured starting subset gives the later search a better initial arrangement than the task’s baseline. The objective is lower star discrepancy: more even coverage of the unit cube.

gains.title: Direct search toward weak coverage
gains.summary: Use exact discrepancy information to guide candidate changes.
gains.detail: Directed search concentrates proposals on the regions that limit the current subset’s coverage. Exact scoring determines whether a candidate improves the objective.

gains.title: Screen the directed proposals
gains.summary: Spend expensive scoring work on more promising candidate changes.
gains.detail: The candidate adds screening to the directed-search process. This reorganizes how the fixed computation budget is spent while retaining the discrepancy objective.

gains.title: Let search cross local barriers
gains.summary: Introduce annealing into directed subset search.
gains.detail: Annealed search can explore beyond immediately improving swaps. The implementation retains the best subset found, rather than assuming the last visited state is best.

gains.title: Search near critical boundaries
gains.summary: Focus swaps where they can change the worst-covered regions.
gains.detail: Boundary-focused local proposals target the points that influence critical coverage errors. Occasional global proposals preserve broader exploration.

gains.title: Make critical-region scoring native
gains.summary: Accelerate exact discrepancy work in the search loop.
gains.detail: A native critical-search implementation reduces the cost of evaluating proposals. Faster scoring makes additional search possible within the unchanged task budget.

gains.title: Use the saved time for deeper search
gains.summary: Combine native scoring with a more extensive annealed search.
gains.detail: The selected implementation combines an exact native discrepancy kernel, fused proposal scoring, and deeper search. It explores more candidate subsets within the task’s runtime limit.

tasks.title: Extract useful structure from categorical IDs.
tasks.goal: Rank employee access requests by learning relationships between categorical fields and pooled unlabeled records.

gains.title: Turn category co-occurrence into features
gains.summary: Describe how pairs of categorical values occur together.
gains.detail: Conditional pair features add relational information beyond treating each category ID independently. The feature construction uses the permitted pooled records.

gains.title: Combine two complementary models
gains.summary: Ensemble two 700-tree models using conditional features.
gains.detail: The candidate distributes learning across two model seeds. Its measured result reflects the tradeoff between model diversity, tree allocation, and the available runtime.

gains.title: Spread the tree budget across three models
gains.summary: Use a three-model ensemble with 466 trees per model.
gains.detail: Changing ensemble size and per-model depth of training tests whether more complementary predictions improve ranking. The conditional features remain part of the learned representation.

gains.title: Expand the conditional ensemble
gains.summary: Combine nine models with 466 trees each.
gains.detail: The larger ensemble builds on conditional category features. The saved checkpoint records the resulting validation and hidden-test ranking quality under the task’s limits.

gains.title: Choose less-redundant pair features
gains.summary: Select supported conditional features using residual information.
gains.detail: The selector aims to retain useful category relationships with less residual redundancy. It builds on the existing ensemble rather than replacing the learned ranking approach.

gains.title: Add another ensemble member
gains.summary: Extend the model combination to ten 466-tree members.
gains.detail: The retained feature and ensemble design is evaluated with one additional member. This checkpoint produces a small validation improvement; the chart retains the measured size of that change.

gains.title: Rebalance ensemble width and tree allocation
gains.summary: Combine eleven models with 424 trees each.
gains.detail: The final selected configuration redistributes the ensemble’s tree allocation. The headline for this task is 24-hour hidden-test AUARC, which accounts for the quality and timing of the whole selected trajectory.

tasks.title: Recover uncertainty from the optimization stream.
tasks.goal: Estimate parameter uncertainty from a model’s optimization trajectory, using the task’s structured covariance setting.

gains.title: Estimate covariance from the model structure
gains.summary: Replace the generic starting estimator with a plug-in Lyapunov approach.
gains.detail: Use estimated structural quantities to form the covariance estimate. This changes the estimation method rather than relying only on longer averaging of the optimization trajectory.

gains.title: Exploit equicorrelation
gains.summary: Estimate the shared correlation structure directly.
gains.detail: The candidate uses the task’s equicorrelation structure to reduce the estimation problem. A small set of structural estimates replaces a more general covariance representation.

gains.title: Separate the pilot from the estimation tail
gains.summary: Estimate correlation on a disjoint pilot and use full-stream noise information.
gains.detail: Use a 3,000-record pilot for variance-weighted correlation estimation, then freeze the pilot weighting before processing the tail. Full-stream ordinary-least-squares residuals provide the noise estimate.

gains.title: Correct finite-sample bias
gains.summary: Add a curvature-based correction to the structured estimator.
gains.detail: A second-derivative correction addresses finite-sample bias in the structural estimates. The implementation retains the disjoint pilot and the parallel/orthogonal covariance decomposition.

nearTies.criterion: Absolute relative difference of at most 5% in final hidden-test raw metric, from the initial CPU campaign.

tasks.title: Selecting Useful Documents for Active Learning
tasks.teaser: Better examples for each labeling round.
tasks.approach: Confidence, diversity, and a shortlist that changes with the round.
tasks.goal: Shrink the unlabeled document pool before each labeling round while preserving the examples that help the final classifier.

gains.title: Let a public teacher guide the shortlist
gains.summary: Use teacher confidence to select informative candidates from the document pool.
gains.detail: The first retained improvement introduces a teacher trained on permitted public data. Its confidence scores guide balanced selection from the two ends of the ranking, before the downstream learner chooses examples to label.

gains.title: Retain 500 candidates for the later rounds
gains.summary: Give the acquisition model a compact, higher-quality shortlist.
gains.detail: Keep 500 candidates in rounds one through four, retaining the existing teacher. Public comparisons tested shortlist sizes before the candidate was submitted to the original grader.

gains.title: Start with a smaller initial pool
gains.summary: Use 125 initial candidates, then expand to 500.
gains.detail: The initial round uses a deterministic 125-candidate selection. Subsequent rounds retain 500 candidates, balancing a focused start with more choice as labels accumulate.

gains.title: Add a diversity cap
gains.summary: Prevent a confident shortlist from being dominated by one document cluster.
gains.detail: Partition projected document features into 128 clusters and cap selection at eight documents per cluster when feasible. The policy retains balanced teacher-confidence ranking and falls back to the incumbent selection when the cap cannot fill the shortlist.

gains.title: Widen the capped shortlist
gains.summary: Increase the supervised shortlist from 500 to 625 candidates.
gains.detail: Give the downstream acquisition model more choice while preserving the teacher, initial pool, cluster partition, and eight-per-cluster cap. The change improves the recorded validation score.

gains.title: Change retention across the rounds
gains.summary: Focus the first supervised round and widen the final one.
gains.detail: Replace fixed supervised retention with the schedule 125 → 500 → 625 → 625 → 750. Early rounds filter more tightly; the last round leaves more options for the acquisition model.

gains.title: Keep the middle round focused
gains.summary: Reduce the third shortlist from 625 to 500.
gains.detail: The schedule becomes 125 → 500 → 500 → 625 → 750. Teacher filtering stays stronger for one additional round while the later shortlists still widen.

gains.title: Refine the later-round shortlist
gains.summary: Increase the fourth-round shortlist to 687 candidates.
gains.detail: The final selected policy uses 125 → 500 → 500 → 687 → 750, with the same confidence ranking and cluster occupancy cap. The recorded source contains this schedule; its final validation score selects checkpoint 22.

tasks.title: High throughput data imputation
tasks.teaser: Recover missing values within a tight compute budget.
tasks.approach: Conditional estimates, residual models, and selective extra work.
tasks.goal: Fill missing table values accurately while respecting the task’s per-call computation budget.

gains.title: Use iterative ridge prediction
gains.summary: Predict missing values from the other columns.
gains.detail: The first retained candidate replaces the starting imputation method with iterative ridge regression. Repeated column predictions use relationships among observed features to improve reconstruction.

gains.title: Combine linear and nonlinear predictions
gains.summary: Ensemble ridge regression with histogram-based boosting.
gains.detail: A boosted model adds nonlinear relationships to the ridge estimate. The candidate combines their predictions rather than relying on a single imputation method.

gains.title: Weight the combined predictions
gains.summary: Adjust how strongly the ridge and boosted models contribute.
gains.detail: The weighted ensemble refines the balance between the two prediction paths. It is evaluated as a complete imputation implementation under the unchanged task budget.

gains.title: Strengthen the boosted component
gains.summary: Increase the capacity of the weighted histogram-based model.
gains.detail: The checkpoint refines the nonlinear component while keeping the weighted ridge/boosting approach. Its measured reconstruction quality improves over the preceding selected candidate.

gains.title: Model what the Gaussian estimate misses
gains.summary: Fit boosted residuals on top of Gaussian conditional means.
gains.detail: Pairwise covariance with positive-semidefinite regularization provides conditional means. Leave-one-out predictions on observed targets provide residuals for histogram-based boosting, with one matrix inverse per row.

gains.title: Learn how much residual correction to apply
gains.summary: Calibrate the blend using held-out observed targets.
gains.detail: Fit the residual model on 80% of observed targets, estimate a regularized blend coefficient on the remaining 20%, then refit using all observed targets. The strength of the correction adapts to the available evidence.

gains.title: Give the residual model its conditional anchor
gains.summary: Include the Gaussian target estimate as an extra predictor.
gains.detail: The conditional mean becomes an explicit feature for the residual model. This lets the nonlinear correction use both the raw predictors and the estimate it is correcting.

gains.title: Spend the forest budget where it fits
gains.summary: Add an ExtraTrees residual ensemble on smaller tables.
gains.detail: Use a computational-size gate based on rows times squared columns. Smaller tables receive the extra residual ensemble; larger tables keep the existing Gaussian/boosting anchor so the additional work stays bounded.

gains.title: Fill predictors conditionally before residual fitting
gains.summary: Use target-excluded Gaussian-filled features inside the existing work gate.
gains.detail: For smaller tables, feed conditionally filled predictors to the histogram-boosting/ExtraTrees residual ensemble. Larger tables retain the established raw-predictor branch. The routing depends on table size, not dataset identity.

gains.title: Fit independent features concurrently
gains.summary: Use four in-process workers for residual fitting.
gains.detail: Parallelize independent residual fits while preserving estimator parameters, seeds, feature order, covariance calculations, and routing. This changes how the existing work is scheduled within the call budget.

gains.title: Allocate extra fitting selectively
gains.summary: Allow longer boosting where observed-target evidence supports it.
gains.detail: The staged-capacity candidate adapts additional fitting to individual targets. It balances a more capable correction against the risk that extra computation leaves less work completed before the deadline.

tasks.title: Training reliable control policies under tight budgets
tasks.teaser: Learn the dynamics, then plan the control.
tasks.approach: System identification followed by controllers matched to the dynamics.
tasks.goal: Train reliable controllers from scratch using only the permitted interaction data and a tight training budget.

gains.title: Identify the pendulum before planning
gains.summary: Learn dynamics from transitions, then solve a control problem.
gains.detail: Estimate physical coordinates, dynamics, delay, and cost from 19,200 permitted transitions. Bellman grid planning then produces a pendulum controller. The policy uses learned information rather than accessing environment internals.

gains.title: Combine swing-up with local stabilization
gains.summary: Add learned cartpole dynamics, energy-based swing-up, and LQR.
gains.detail: The next controller identifies the cartpole geometry and dynamics. Energy-based control handles swing-up, while a linear-quadratic regulator stabilizes the system near the target.

gains.title: Match controllers to the remaining systems
gains.summary: Extend the identified-model approach to reacher and linear systems.
gains.detail: Learn reacher geometry, dynamics, and targets for inverse-kinematics/proportional-derivative control, and use learned linear-system dynamics and rewards for LQR. The selected checkpoint reaches a 100% reliable-task rate on both recorded splits.

tasks.title: Reducing Search in Integer Optimization
tasks.teaser: Choose branches that shrink the solver’s search.
tasks.approach: Learn branching decisions from public strong-branching examples.
tasks.goal: Choose branching variables so an integer solver explores fewer nodes. The submitted policy uses the allowed observations rather than calling a solver itself.

gains.title: Combine fractionality with objective information
gains.summary: Use more than a variable’s distance from an integer.
gains.detail: The first retained heuristic incorporates both fractionality and objective information into the branching score. It changes which variable the solver branches on next.

gains.title: Soften the objective weighting
gains.summary: Use square-root cost in the branching score.
gains.detail: A half-power cost weighting changes the balance between objective information and fractionality. The candidate reduces the recorded search-node metric further.

gains.title: Account for pressure from tight constraints
gains.summary: Add graph information from the current LP observation.
gains.detail: Multiply fractionality and square-root cost by square-root tight-row graph pressure. The score uses the legal constraint/variable observations to favor branches that affect tight parts of the problem.

gains.title: Learn from strong-branching examples
gains.summary: Train a predictor on permitted public solver trajectories.
gains.detail: Strong-branching labels are collected during public training, where solver use is permitted. The submitted policy blends a learned score with the heuristic using only the allowed observations at inference time.

gains.title: Learn on the constraint-variable graph
gains.summary: Use a graph model to imitate strong branching.
gains.detail: Represent the integer program as a bipartite graph of constraints and variables. The model learns branching rankings from public labels and replaces the earlier predictor in the deployed policy.

gains.title: Expand training and make graph execution cheaper
gains.summary: Add on-policy labels and use compressed sparse-row matrices.
gains.detail: New public trajectories expand the training data. Switching graph operations to compressed sparse-row storage preserves the checked logits and solve node counts while reducing preparation and forward-pass overhead.

gains.title: Train on deeper search states
gains.summary: Collect examples after the solver has already made decisions.
gains.detail: Fine-tune with public strong-branching examples from deeper states along complete solves. This exposes the model to decisions beyond the beginning of the search.

gains.title: Add competition and movement information
gains.summary: Refine graph rankings with bounded observation-derived descriptors.
gains.detail: The native candidate adds candidate-excluded competition and signed movement residuals to the retained graph policy. The checkpoint records a validation improvement on that cumulative implementation.

gains.title: Widen the learned graph model
gains.summary: Use a 64-wide model trained across public problem shifts.
gains.detail: The wider graph model learns from expanded public strong-branching data. It is a separate selected branch from the preceding residual-descriptor candidate; the mixed evidence did not support combining both changes.

gains.title: Fine-tune the ranking head
gains.summary: Keep the graph trunk fixed and update the prediction head.
gains.detail: The selected checkpoint is control arm C: head-only fine-tuning with the existing supervised loss and a KL anchor to the retained model. It is not the regret-weighted challenger. The architecture and inference operation sequence stay unchanged.
